messages:
alex.t: Heads-up — after last night's RBAC split deploy a handful of customers' embedding requests are being rejected by the chat endpoint (403). I think there's a tag-sync race with KMS metadata.

maria.k: Can you paste a minimal failing curl + reply body?

alex.t: sure:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1","input":"foo"}'

-> 403 Forbidden
{"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"token missing route:embeddings.write"}
```

alex.t: but the same token successfully called embeddings earlier today. Audit shows token_tag cleared intermittently: 
```
2026-03-20T02:12:58Z INFO audit request_id=abc123 path=/v1/embeddings auth.token_tag=null api_key_id=ak_foo
2026-03-20T02:12:58Z INFO auth decision=deny reason=missing_scope expected=embeddings.write
```

kms-bot: KMS rewrap job completed for key=projects/redwood/keys/yk-44 at 2026-03-20T02:13:05Z (job id: rewrap-20260320-02). No errors at storage layer.

sre-oncall: this smells like race between RBAC split + KMS metadata propagation. If token_tag is computed from KMS metadata and that was temporarily unavailable, scope-check would see a null tag and fail.

samir: can we confirm whether per-route scope matcher falls back to legacy allowlist when token_tag missing? IIRC new authz path rejects unless tag present.

jessica: running an audit query now: `select count(*) from audit where auth.token_tag is null and path like '/v1/%' and ts > '2026-03-20T02:00:00Z'` — getting ~42 rows across 6 customers, mostly embedding calls.

alex.t: also noticed pattern: clients using long-lived API keys created before RBAC split are more affected — looks like older keys don't have the new key_tag in KMS metadata until rewrap finishes.

maria.k: mitigation options: 1) force-roll KMS tag propagation (risky), 2) temporarily revert RBAC split to legacy allowlist behavior, 3) batch-update auth service to accept missing token_tag and check legacy tag repository. Thoughts?

sre-oncall: revert RBAC split (option 2) is fastest and safest short-term. We'll revert canary ASAP, block further rewrap jobs until we confirm metadata propagation.

samir: preference for minimal code change -> accept missing token_tag and consult legacy allowlist as fallback (option 3) — but deploy risk. If revert is fast, do that first and then ship a measured fallback fix.

ops-bot: Deploy revert triggered by @sre-oncall — rollback id rb-split-20260320-01. Canary flagged, preflight checks started. :rocket:

alex.t: after rollback, 200 responses resumed for the affected customers. Collecting full testimony and will open follow-up ticket for durable fix.

jessica: filing triage ticket now: ENGSEC-7831 — description: "KMS tag sync race causes null token_tag -> embeddings treated as chat (403) after RBAC split". Assigning to eng-auth and eng-ml infra.

samir: for the long-term we should: 1) add strong audit metric for token_tag null rate, 2) make KMS rewrap orchestrator signal completion before RBAC flags flip, 3) ensure authz has a controlled fallback chain documented.

maria.k: also add automation to revoke/flag any API keys created before policy-change when we do key metadata migrations — better to quarantine and rotate than allow ambiguous state.

alex.t: thanks all. I'll attach sample logs and the list of affected customers to ENGSEC-7831. Follow-up doc should include rollback playbook for RBAC feature gates. :+1:
